name: IT team · demo/up.sh has no executable test — nothing can verify --list-providers / --ref
description:
Finding from the QA gate on card `2639c296` (demo/up.sh --list-providers / --ref documented but not implemented).

## The gap
`demo/up.sh` is the demo's single entry point, but nothing in the repo executes it. The QA tools can map and run tests only for languages declared in `qa_policy.suites` (today: none, `tests.no-suite`), so a change to `demo/up.sh` can never be evidenced: `qa_review_changes` on this card returned `changed_files: 0` (path-filter bug `f3e1dd0c`) and a whole-repo run gives `test_files: 0 / mapped_sources: 0`. Static reading of the code is currently the only check available, and static reading cannot prove a CLI flag works.

## What to do
Add a shell-level smoke test for the argument surface of `demo/up.sh` that runs without Docker and without touching `.env` — e.g. `demo/tests/up.bats` (bats-core) or `demo/tests/test_up.sh` with `set -eu`.

Minimum cases:
1. `./up.sh --help` → exit 0, prints `Usage:`.
2. `./up.sh --list-providers` → exit 0, stdout contains all 8 presets (`openai deepseek gemini openrouter mistral groq ollama custom`) and the model ids the script writes for them; **no** `.env` created/modified.
3. `./up.sh --ref <tag>` / `CODX_JUNIOR_REF=<tag>` → the resolved image reference contains `<tag>` and `latest` is not used.
4. `./up.sh --bogus` → exit 1, stderr/`Unknown option`, usage printed (the `*)` fallback is not shadowed by the new cases).
5. Guard against the regression this card was filed for: each option advertised in the `usage()` text is accepted by the parser (parse the `--flag` tokens out of usage and fail if one is not handled).

Then declare the runner so the gate can execute it:
`qa_policy.suites = {"shell": {"command": ["bats", "demo/tests/"]}}` (or `["bash","demo/tests/test_up.sh"]`), coordinated with `d1ba037a` which owns the pytest suite declaration.

## Acceptance criteria
- `qa_run_tests(suite="shell")` (or the declared name) → `decision: allow`, tests executed > 0, 0 failures.
- `qa_review_changes(paths=["demo/up.sh"], scope="all")` → `changed_files: 1`, `mapped_sources: 1` (or the path is explicitly declared in `qa_policy.ignore_paths` with a dated reason — not silently).
- Deleting `--list-providers` from the parser makes at least one test red (prove the suite bites).
- No test touches the network or Docker; the suite runs in seconds in a shift seat.

## Notes
- Do not "fix" this by adding `demo/` to `qa_policy.ignore_paths` without a dated user-approved reason: `demo/up.sh` is the demo's entry point, exactly the code the 21 Nov demo depends on.
- Owner profile `qa_automation` does not exist in this project's catalogue; this is filed for `software_developer`.

## Increment 1 — executable test for `demo/up.sh` (card scope only)

**Changed files (1 new, nothing else):**
- `A` **`demo/tests/test_up.sh`** — new, **308 lines, +308/-0** (confirmed by `project_changes(paths="demo/")` at 2026-11-19T14:0xZ: `3 file(s), +385/-7` = my new file plus the two pre-existing `demo/up.sh` / `demo/README.md` modifications from `2639c296`, which this card does **not** touch).
- `demo/up.sh` — **not modified** by this card. `demo/README.md` — **not modified** (documenting the test is a separate, reviewable change; not done to keep the increment one-thing).

**What the test asserts** (5 cases + 2 hygiene checks, TAP-like `ok N - …` output, exit 0 / 1):
1. `:123` `--help` → exit 0, prints `Usage: ./up.sh`.
2. `:139` `--list-providers` → exit 0, prints the preset table, **runs with no `docker` on PATH** (the point is that listing must work on a host without Docker; the parser handles it before the gate at `up.sh:138`).
3. `:189` `--ref v1.2.3`, `CODX_JUNIOR_REF`, `--ref main` → image tag resolves to `codxjunior/codx-junior:v1.2.3` / `…:main` instead of the rolling `:demo`.
4. `:228` unknown option → non-zero **and** `Unknown option` on stderr.
5. `:251` **usage-vs-parser guard** — every `--flag` token extracted from `--help` is fed to the parser and must not come back `Unknown option`. This is the direct regression guard for `2639c296` (`--list-providers` was advertised at `up.sh:42` and absent from the `case` at `up.sh:101-111`; nothing noticed).
6. `:288` the suite leaves `demo/.env` byte-identical (`env_fingerprint`, `:68`).
7. `:296` the suite creates nothing new inside `demo/` (`demo_listing`, `:77`).

**Design constraint (why it is safe to run anywhere):** cases 1, 2 and 4 exit inside the argument parser, before the docker gate (`up.sh:138`) and before `.env` creation (`up.sh:169`), so they run against the **real** `demo/up.sh`. Cases 3 and 5 cross the gate and rewrite `.env`, so they run against a throw-away sandbox copy of `demo/` (`run_sut_copy`, `:116`) with a **stub `docker` first on PATH** — no pull, no container, no network.

**Validation evidence**
- Command to run: `bash demo/tests/test_up.sh` (no executable bit needed, runnable from any cwd — `:19-20`).
- Expected result: one `ok N - …` line per check, final `N check(s), 0 failure(s)` on stdout, **exit code 0**.
- **NOT EXECUTED from this seat.** There is no shell/command tool in my toolset; running it is impossible here, and I will not present a static reading as a test result. What I *can* state as evidence is static and line-referenced:
  - the file exists and reads back as 308 lines (fresh read at 2026-11-19T14:0xZ, not from memory);
  - the assertions above are cited by the line numbers where they live;
  - `set -euo pipefail` (`:25`) plus `trap cleanup EXIT` (`:33`) — the tmpdir is always removed;
  - the test creates its own sandbox under `$TMP` and never writes inside the repository, which is itself asserted at `:296`.

**Residual risks a reviewer must check with a real shell (I cannot):**
- `:255` runs `run … ; grep …` inside a command substitution under `set -e`; if `--help` ever returns non-zero the assignment aborts instead of failing one check.
- the stub `docker` must satisfy **every** compose call reached by the boolean flags `--build`, `--dev`, `--no-wait`, `--non-interactive` (case 5 exercises them); a stub gap shows up as `not ok`, not as a false pass.
- case 5 derives its flag list by regex from `--help`, so any future prose token starting with `--` adds a check. Current extraction from `up.sh:39-58` yields exactly the 13 advertised flags.

**Known remaining gap, deliberately not closed here:** the test is executable but **not declared in `qa_policy`**, so no gate runs it automatically — that is card `d1ba037a` (blocked on `248d0a54`). This card makes the flags *verifiable*; it does not make them *gated*.

**Scope discipline:** `2639c296` (the `up.sh` change itself) untouched; `b9aaf03c` untouched; no branch, no commit. Moving this card to **Review** at progress 70 — the reviewer needs one command run, nothing designed.

## Static verification of `demo/tests/test_up.sh` — each assertion traced to the line that produces it

Still no execution from this seat (no shell tool). What follows replaces opinion with a line-by-line trace, so the suite's expectations are not guesses:

1. **stdout vs stderr.** `log()` prints to stdout (`up.sh:133`, `printf` with no `>&2`), so `out_has` (`test_up.sh:62`) really does match `Pulling codxjunior/codx-junior:v1.2.3...` from `up.sh:265`. The assertions at `test_up.sh:199` and `:206` are sound for that reason alone.
2. **Tag resolution.** `--ref v1.2.3` → `up.sh:248-249` (`^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+`) → pinned tag; `--ref main` and `CODX_JUNIOR_REF=v2.3.4` respectively → `up.sh:251` rolling `:demo` and `:249` pinned. Matches cases `test_up.sh:190`, `:212`, `:220`.
3. **Sandbox cannot leak into the repository.** `run_sut_copy` cds to `${SANDBOX}/demo` (`test_up.sh:117`); `PROJECTS_PATH` defaults to `./projects` (`up.sh:194`) and is then `mkdir -p` + `cd` (`up.sh:224-225`), i.e. created inside `${TMP}` and removed by `cleanup` (`test_up.sh:32`). The `demo/` listing snapshot (`:76-77`, `:288-302`) stays valid.
4. **`.env` path cannot fail.** `demo/.env.example` exists in the tree, so `up.sh:169` `cp` succeeds on the sandbox copy; the repository `.env` is fingerprinted (`test_up.sh:68-74`) and asserted unchanged (`:181-187`).
5. **Case 3 is fast, not a 2-minute wait.** The stub answers `docker inspect` with `healthy` (`test_up.sh:90`), matched by `up.sh:285-286`, so the health loop breaks on iteration 1 (no `sleep 2`); `docker exec` returns 0 (`test_up.sh:91`) so the provider step (`up.sh:299-301`) and summary (`:303`) cannot fail either → `rc=0`, matching `test_up.sh:192`.
6. **Why case 2 may use a docker stub that fails on purpose.** `--help` / `--list-providers` exit inside the parser (`up.sh:114-115`), before the docker gate (`:138`) and before `.env` creation (`:169`) — that is precisely the property `test_up.sh:101-106` and `:140` test.

### Residual risks — unchanged and on the record

- **Nothing above was executed.** The command is `bash demo/tests/test_up.sh`; the line `N check(s), 0 failure(s)` is the evidence QA must paste into `140c8fb0`. Static tracing can prove an assertion *matches its target string*, it cannot prove the suite's own syntax.
- **`demo/tests/test_up.sh` is untracked** (`project_changes(demo/)`: `A demo/tests/test_up.sh (+308/-0)`). A QA run in a clean checkout will not see the file until it is staged. Staging/committing is a PM decision and outside this card's increment; flagged so it is not lost between `716c63f8` (Review) and `140c8fb0` (verdict, 2026-11-20T17:00Z).

## Tail of the suite verified — the file is a usable gate, and nothing in the tree hides it

Last two checks of this increment, both from fresh reads this turn.

### 1. Exit-code contract (`demo/tests/test_up.sh:304-308`)

```
304| printf '\n%d check(s), %d failure(s)\n' "${CHECKED}" "${FAILED}"
305| if [[ ${FAILED} -ne 0 ]]; then
306|     exit 1
307| fi
308| exit 0
```

So a CI job or a manual QA run can gate on the **exit status alone**, and the
`ok N - …` / `not ok N - …` lines (`:38-47`) are TAP-shaped, so a failure names
the exact assertion instead of only a count.

### 2. The two "did the suite damage the tree?" guards are the last checks

Before the summary line, the suite asserts:
- `:289-294` — `demo/.env` fingerprint unchanged (`env_fingerprint` `:68-74`);
- `:296-302` — the top-level listing of `demo/` is byte-identical before/after (`demo_listing`, `:76-…`).

That ordering matters: the guards run *after* every case, including the
`--ref`/`--dev` runs that reach `.env` creation and `mkdir -p ./projects` in
`demo/up.sh` (`:169`, `:224-225`). Because they are last, a case that leaks into
the real `demo/` fails the suite rather than passing silently.

### 3. Nothing excludes the new file — verified, not assumed

`project_read_file([".gitignore", "demo/.gitignore"])` → **both "File not found"**,
i.e. there is no ignore rule that would keep `demo/tests/test_up.sh` out of the
index. `project_changes(demo/)` still reports it as `A demo/tests/test_up.sh
(+308/-0)` next to `M demo/README.md (+32/-5)` and `M demo/up.sh (+45/-2)` —
3 files, +385/−7, and nothing outside `demo/`.

### What is still NOT done, and why it is not mine to do

- **It has never been executed.** `bash demo/tests/test_up.sh` needs a shell; this
  seat has none (root cause card `f64f76ea`). Everything above is static tracing:
  each assertion is tied to the line of `demo/up.sh` that produces the string, but
  "the assertions target the right text" is not "the script runs green".
- **It is not staged/committed.** Tracking it would mean committing the whole
  working tree, which also carries `2639c296`'s `demo/up.sh` hunk and someone
  else's `demo/README.md` edit — that is a review decision, not a shift decision,
  and it would widen this card's scope.

Acceptance for whoever takes this from Review: run `bash demo/tests/test_up.sh`
from the repo root, expect `exit 0` and `N check(s), 0 failure(s)`; a green run
*with* the `--list-providers` case passing is the proof that `2639c296` is fixed.
If it fails, the `not ok` line names the assertion — paste it back here rather
than re-opening `2639c296`'s scope.

## QA verdict: block — the suite exists, the runner does not

- **Scope:** Review of the working tree, `demo/` only: `demo/up.sh` (+45/−2), `demo/tests/test_up.sh` (new, 308 lines), `demo/README.md` (+32/−5).
- **Evidence (gate, quoted):**
  - `qa_run_tests(suite="shell")` → `decision: block`, `[high] tests.no-suite` — *"Add a pytest/npm test setup, or declare the command in `qa_policy.suites`"*. **0 tests executed.**
  - `qa_run_tests(suite="auto")` → `decision: require_approval`, `[medium] tests.run-error` — the only declared suite `pytest:demo` exits 1 with `passed 0 / failed 0 / errors 0 / skipped 0` in 0.0 s. The default suite is not merely empty, it is broken.
  - `qa_review_changes(paths=["demo/up.sh","demo/tests/test_up.sh"])` → `allow`, findings 0 — **`changed_files: 0`**. Rejected as evidence: this is the known false pass `f3e1dd0c` on a diff that `project_changes(paths=["demo/"])` reports as 3 files, +385/−7. A green with zero files reviewed proves nothing.
  - `qa_plan(scope="all")` → `suites: pytest:demo`, `mapped_tests: 0`, `coverage: no report`.
- **Failing test ids:** none — nothing ran. Silence is not a pass.
- **What is actually good (static, credited):** `demo/tests/test_up.sh` is real and well-built — TAP-like output, `set -euo pipefail`, temp sandbox, stub `docker` on PATH (no Docker/network), and it bites where it matters: `--list-providers` with a `nodocker` PATH (proves the flag never consults Docker), `--ref v1.2.3` → `codxjunior/codx-junior:v1.2.3` **and** must not fall back to `:demo`, `CODX_JUNIOR_REF=v2.3.4`, `--ref main` keeps `:demo`, `--bogus` → rc 1 + `Unknown option: --bogus` + usage, `.env` untouched, `demo/` listing unchanged, and the case-5 guard that every flag advertised by `usage()` is accepted by the parser — the exact regression that produced `2639c296`. Static reading also confirms the fix is present (`--list-providers) usage_providers; exit 0 ;;`, `usage_providers()` at `up.sh:66`, pinned-tag branch at `up.sh:246-248`).
- **Exact gap (the only blocker):** the suite is not declared, so no gate can reach it. Add to the project QA policy:
  `suites.shell = { "kind": "shell", "cwd": "demo", "command": ["bash", "tests/test_up.sh"] }`
  and repair or drop the broken `pytest:demo` default. Owner: `d1ba037a`, not this card's content.
- **Acceptance to re-verify:** `qa_run_tests(suite="shell")` returns `passed: true`, exit 0, **and** reports a non-zero check count; then a negative control (comment out the `--list-providers)` arm) must turn the run red with `not ok ... advertised in usage() but rejected by the parser`. A suite that cannot go red is not a gate.
- **Card moved back to Working** with this gap. I edited no product file and no test.

You cannot run before the suite exists.** Your acceptance criteria require `qa_run_tests(suite="shell")` → `allow` with tests executed > 0, and your Notes say the runner declaration is *"coordinated with `d1ba037a` which owns the pytest suite declaration"*. `d1ba037a` had 20 Nov 16:00Z; it is now **23 Nov 10:00Z**, followed by `5ee9dbfa` at 12:00Z. Waking you on 21 Nov would have guaranteed a fourth session ending in "suite not declared".

**2. Your old wake was Saturday.** 21 Nov 2026 is a Saturday. That was acceptable for post-demo work when nothing upstream had moved; it is not acceptable now that you have a hard, dated prerequisite.

New slot **Mon 23 Nov 14:00Z**, after both QA-infra cards. Chain: `248d0a54` (20 Nov 16:00Z) → `d1ba037a` (23 Nov 10:00Z) → `5ee9dbfa` (23 Nov 12:00Z) → **you** (23 Nov 14:00Z).

## PM correction (shift #7, 2026-11-19) — your Notes contain a false statement, and it put you on a seat that cannot run you

Your Notes say: *"Owner profile `qa_automation` does not exist in this project's catalogue; this is filed for `software_developer`."*

**That is wrong, and I verified it directly this shift.** `list_profiles(query="qa_automation", include_inherited=true)` returns it with `category: "project"`, `project_id: "194562fb-8850-4f0c-bfeb-46d2ecfb82f8"` (this project), `has_content: true`, path `/…/api/codx/junior/profiles/qa_automation/qa_automation.profile`. It not only exists, it is a **first-class project profile** — and it is currently assigned to `d1ba037a`, `5ee9dbfa` and `140c8fb0`.

That false note had a real cost. Your acceptance criteria require `qa_run_tests(suite="shell")` → `allow` with **tests executed > 0**. The seat you were on cannot do that:

| Seat | Writes files | Runs a suite | Executes a shell command |
|---|---|---|---|
| `software_developer` (your old seat) | yes (via linked `file_editor`) | **no** — holds no `qa_*` tool | **no** |
| `qa_automation` | yes (`project_write_file`, `apply_file_changes`) | **yes** (`qa_run_tests`, `qa_review_changes`) | no |
| `devops` | — | — | **yes** (`docker_exec`) |

So you were armed to *write* a test and then prove it green on a seat with no way to run anything. Same defect class as `4f055e99` (`profiles: []`) and `b9aaf03c` (`web_master` on a card needing Docker) — the third instance this shift.

**Profiles corrected → `["qa_automation","devops"]`. Division of work, so this does not become shared ownership:**
- **`qa_automation` is the owner.** Writes `demo/tests/`, declares the runner in `qa_policy.suites`, and produces the acceptance evidence with `qa_run_tests(suite="shell")`.
- **`devops` is the execution channel only.** If the suite needs a real shell (`bash demo/tests/test_up.sh` with the repo mounted), `docker_exec` is the only route in this project. It runs the command you wrote; it does not redesign the test.
- `software_developer` may still be used for authoring the shell script, but it must never be the seat that signs the suite off.

**Unchanged:** the minimum cases (including case 5 — parsing the `--flag` tokens out of `usage()` and failing on any unhandled one; that is the regression that created this card), the no-Docker/no-network constraint on the *tests themselves* (they must run without Docker even though `devops` executes them), the prohibition on silencing this via `qa_policy.ignore_paths`, and the new wake **23 Nov 14:00Z** after `d1ba037a` (10:00Z) and `5ee9dbfa` (12:00Z).
